t: The last sentence of section 22 (b) (9) and the last sentence of section 22 (b) (10) of the Internal Revenue Code (relating to exclusion of income from discharge of indebtedness) are hereby amended by striking out “1947” and inserting in lieu thereof “1949”.

fable.w: This section merely extends a date in Internal Revenue Code provisions on the exclusion of income from discharge of indebtedness. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: are hereby amended by striking out “1947” and inserting in lieu thereof “1949”

opus.w: This section only replaces the year "1947" with "1949" in two provisions of the Internal Revenue Code about excluding income from discharged debt. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision: there is no comment period, rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. Reading Yes would mean importing procedures that may exist in the amended code but are not in the text of this section.
opus.b: **Analysis:** This section only changes a date from 1947 to 1949 in two sentences of the Internal Revenue Code about excluding income from discharged debt. One could read it as Yes because the underlying provisions may involve Treasury regulations or elections by taxpayers. That reading fails because the section itself sets up no regulation, consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. It is a purely technical amendment.
